title: The ban stops the market from finding cheaper and faster routes to nuclear, such as small modular reactors
oneLiner: A prohibition rules out every future design, not just today's large plants.
body: Cost and timeline estimates for nuclear are estimates for large reactors built once. Small modular designs promise factory production, shorter builds and smaller sites, and several are in licensing overseas. A legislated ban means no Australian proponent can test those promises against local conditions, however the technology develops.
contextBackground: This is the positive case for repeal that does not depend on building a large plant soon: it treats the ban as a restriction on what the market may discover. It is the argument most often made by people who are agnostic about whether nuclear will ever pencil out in Australia.
contextDisagreement: The reply is that small modular reactors do not yet exist commercially in comparable countries, so the option being preserved is speculative. Whether that matters depends on how one values keeping options open.

otherClaim.title: Australia should repeal its federal ban on nuclear power generation

claimItself.title: Australia should repeal its federal ban on nuclear power generation
claimItself.oneLiner: Whether the 1998 prohibition on nuclear power plants should be lifted. Repeal is a separate question from whether anyone would then build one.
claimItself.body: Two federal Acts prohibit the approval of a nuclear power plant anywhere in Australia. Repealing them would allow proposals to be assessed on their merits under the ordinary environmental, safety and planning regimes. Whether a plant would then be commercially viable, or built in time to matter, is argued below.

otherClaim.title: No commercial small modular reactor has yet operated in a Western country, and the first United States project was cancelled in 2023

claimItself.title: No commercial small modular reactor has yet operated in a Western country, and the first United States project was cancelled in 2023
claimItself.oneLiner: The designs being licensed overseas remain unbuilt; the most advanced US project collapsed on cost.
claimItself.body: Small modular reactors operate in Russia and China under state programs. In the United States, the NuScale project for a Utah utility consortium was cancelled in November 2023 after its estimated power price rose and subscribers withdrew. No Western SMR has reached commercial operation.
